Subject: Elmwood RFP — KMS, key rotation, audit logs and evidence needed

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of Elmwood's procurement RFP and our security review, the security team has a short list of artifacts we need to validate HIPAA readiness and PHI handling. Can you confirm the following and provide supporting evidence where possible?

1) Key management: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM-backed keys? Please include key rotation policy, KMS provider(s), and whether keys for PHI are exported or non-exportable.
2) Audit logging: examples of access logs showing read/write to PHI-related endpoints, retention windows, and the format of event records.
3) Data flow diagram showing where PHI may persist or be cached (non-persistent vs. stored) and any egress controls.
4) BAA status and an example of our preferred redline path or any exceptions we should be aware of.

If you have a one-page artifact bundle or a short recording we can review that would help accelerate our security committee sign-off. We need the materials by COB Friday to stay on our procurement timeline.

Attached: Elmwood_RFP_Attach.pdf (pdf) — our checklist.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Elmwood Health

Subject: Re: Elmwood RFP — KMS, key rotation, audit logs and evidence needed

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and then I'll attach our artifact bundle:

1) KMS: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments. Keys used for PHI are configured as non-exportable by default when using HSM/KMS CMKs.
2) Audit logging: We maintain tamper-evident audit logs (immutable append-only storage) with customizable retention; standard retention is 90 days for hosted and configurable to 7 years for Dedicated/Private. Logs include event type, actor, resource, request_id, and full request path.
3) Data flow: Our hosted API performs ephemeral KV caching for latency; PHI is not persisted to long-term storage unless customer enables storage features. We have network egress controls and region pinning.
4) BAA: Redwood executes a standard BAA; we can share a proposed redline.

I've attached a short artifact bundle: Redwood_HIPAA_Summary.pdf (pdf), redwood_kms_overview.pdf (pdf). Happy to walk through live — propose a 30-min security call tomorrow or Thursday.

Jonas Weber

Hi Alyssa / Raj,

Following up with the artifacts Jonas promised. See the responses below and attached sample evidence. If you prefer a short walkthrough, we can schedule 20–30 minutes Monday.

1) Key management and KMS evidence
- Supported modes: Hosted (Redwood-managed keys), CMK via AWS KMS / GCP KMS, and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private.
- Non-exportable: When CMK/HSM mode is selected for PHI workloads, keys are marked non-exportable and operations require KMS/HSM calls; we do not persist raw key material in our control plane.
- Rotation: default rotation cadence is 90 days for service-managed keys; for CMK customers we recommend provider-managed rotation (customer-configured). Attached: redwood_kms_overview.pdf (overview) and KMS_key_rotation_table.csv (rotation matrix).

2) Audit logging
- Format: JSON lines with fields: timestamp, request_id, actor_id, action, resource_path, response_code, bytes_transferred. Sample entry attached in audit_log_sample.txt.
- Retention: Hosted — 90 days (configurable); Dedicated/Private — configurable to customer requirements (7+ years supported). Logs are stored in immutable buckets with SHA-256 chain validation for tamper evidence.

3) Data flow and PHI handling
- PHI handling: API requests are processed in-memory; we use ephemeral KV cache which is cleared per-session unless customer enables persistent storage. Persistent storage for long-term data is only available in Dedicated/Private.
- Egress and region controls: customers can pin region or restrict egress via VPC and our private deployments. See attached diagram (also uploaded to the Drive link).

4) BAA and contract path
- Redwood executes a BAA for customers handling PHI. We can accept reasonable redlines. I uploaded a proposed redline to the shared drive (link below). We also have a DocuSign-ready version if you prefer.

Attachments: KMS_key_rotation_table.csv, audit_log_sample.txt (sanitized), redwood_kms_overview.pdf

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/elmwood/Redwood-BAA-Proposed-Redline
DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/elmwood/baaredline-12345

Let me know the two items you need prioritized and we can follow up immediately.

Thanks,

Monica / Jonas —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the artifacts — very helpful. A couple of clarifying items before we close the security review:

1) For hosted customers, can we get a short statement that keys for PHI can be configured as CMK non-exportable (we saw the language but need a signed statement for procurement).
2) Can you confirm whether audit log export supports continuous streaming to our SIEM (we use Splunk Cloud) and whether that stream supports encryption-in-transit and mutual TLS?

If you can provide those two short confirmations (one-paragraph each) we can get to our legal and the InfoSec committee. If everything checks out we'll circulate the BAA redline internally and come back with any final contract notes.

Thanks again — aiming to finalize this week.
